=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:81 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore accepts any `https://github.com/` origin instead of verifying it belongs to the authorized workflow repository, so an editor can redirect the origin and receive `GH_TOKEN`.
  WHY: The contract tests change the origin to an attacker-controlled repository and expect restore to fail without injecting the token; the helper accepts the URL and injects the token.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:19-54 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide does not validate `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` or reject pre-existing `remote.origin.pushurl` and `url.*.pushInsteadOf` redirects.
  WHY: The contract tests expect hide to fail on missing trusted repository identity and redirected push destinations; without these checks, credentials can remain exposed to redirected pushes.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:76-83 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore does not reject editor-added push URLs or `pushInsteadOf` rewrites, or multiple `remote.origin.url` entries, before injecting the token.
  WHY: The contract tests expect restore to reject these changed or ambiguous push destinations without injecting credentials.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:85-92 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore writes the original extraheader key without verifying or scoping it to the authorized origin, allowing a generic or untrusted GitHub key to receive the token.
  WHY: The contract tests require origin-scoped restoration and rejection of untrusted extraheader scopes; restoring a host-wide key can apply credentials to other GitHub repositories.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:61-97 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore injects credentials into each checkout before validating the remaining checkouts.
  WHY: If a later checkout has an invalid origin, earlier checkouts already contain the token, contrary to the all-or-nothing contract test.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:102 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The script exits 0 even when restore has set `failed` or encountered validation and Git command errors.
  WHY: Callers cannot detect an unsuccessful restore and proceed as if credentials were safely restored.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:56-60 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore exits 0 when the marker is missing or empty without the required `reason=marker_missing` diagnostic, and exits 0 when `GH_TOKEN` is unset.
  WHY: The contract tests require the marker diagnostic and a nonzero result when the token is absent; callers otherwise cannot detect that credentials were not restored.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:21-24 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A second hide call exits 0 when an unrestored marker already exists.
  WHY: The existing marker state may be needed to restore credentials, and the contract test requires the second hide call to fail rather than proceed with stale state.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:19-54 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The editor can delete or modify the credential marker because it is stored at an editor-writable path.
  WHY: Restore reads the same marker, so deleting or corrupting it can prevent credential restoration or alter which checkouts are processed.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:2727 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The EXIT trap treats restore as successful when the helper exits 0 despite failed restoration.
  WHY: Subsequent workflow operations proceed without a direct restore-failure signal; the standalone syntax-repair restore step also relies on the helper's exit status.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:38-39 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: Review-autofix running the support script from main excludes workspace files whose filename contains `credential`, so it drops PR-branch edits to `editor_git_credentials.sh`.
  WHY: Changes to the exclusion rule in the PR cannot take effect until they land on main, blocking review autofix from modifying this helper.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:483-491 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `_push_targets` `--repo` heuristic can misclassify a positional as a refspec when Git remote or branch-query commands fail or return unexpected statuses.
  WHY: In those degraded states, the guard may treat a positional as a refspec when Git would treat it as a repository, potentially allowing a push to a merged branch.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:480-495 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When `git remote` or `git show-ref` fails during `--repo` handling, the guard falls through to the refspec path without logging or marking the degradation as uncertain.
  WHY: The guard can silently misclassify bare names in a malformed worktree or when Git is unavailable, potentially allowing a push the user did not intend.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:485-490 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: When a positional is both a configured remote and a local branch, `_push_targets` treats it as a refspec even though Git treats it as the repository.
  WHY: The guard may check the branch instead of the effective remote push target and allow a push to that remote carrying a merged branch.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: AD-1: "Remove credentials only: drop GH_TOKEN, GH_PAT, Telegram and other non-model secrets from the editor's environment at both implement editor launches (main loop and syntax repair). The editor keeps the network access the model needs. Pin this with a contract test."
  expected_change_site: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh` does not validate `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, reject changed origins, push URLs or `pushInsteadOf` rewrites, reject multiple origin URLs, scope restored extraheaders to the verified origin, validate all checkouts before injecting tokens, fail nonzero on errors, or emit the missing-marker diagnostic; contract tests in `tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py` assert these behaviors and are registered in CI; `agents.md` documents that restoration verifies workflow repository identity and fails the editor step on error.
- requirement: AD-1: "Pin this with a contract test."
  expected_change_site: tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The test file (286 lines, 18 test functions) is registered in CI, but scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh does not implement the behaviors; at least 13 tests will fail.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:81 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore accepts any origin matching `^https://github\.com/` without verifying that it belongs to the authorized repository, then injects the workflow token.
  WHY: The contract test changes the origin to `https://github.com/attacker/repo.git` and expects nonzero exit with no token in git config; the helper injects the token and exits 0.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 19-54 (hide action) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Hide does not validate `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, check `remote.origin.pushurl`, or check `url.*.pushInsteadOf` rules.
  WHY: The corresponding contract tests expect hide to fail for missing repository identity and redirected push destinations; it exits 0.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 76-83 (restore origin case) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore does not reject editor-added `remote.origin.pushurl`, `url.*.pushInsteadOf` rewrites, or multiple `remote.origin.url` entries.
  WHY: The corresponding contract tests expect restore to reject these conditions without injecting the token; the helper injects it and exits 0.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:line 102 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The script exits 0 regardless of the `failed` flag.
  WHY: Restore failures are masked, and the EXIT trap and per-attempt restore callers rely on the exit code to detect them.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 85-92 (extraheader restore) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore reuses the original extraheader key instead of deriving a scoped key from the verified origin.
  WHY: The contract test expects an origin-scoped key, but the helper writes a generic key that applies to all GitHub repositories.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 61-97 (restore loop) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore injects credentials sequentially before validating all checkouts.
  WHY: The all-checkouts contract test expects restore to fail without injecting the token into any checkout when a later checkout has an invalid origin.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 85-92 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The extraheader scope validation regex accepts any GitHub path segment, including an attacker-controlled repository path.
  WHY: The untrusted-scope contract test expects restore to fail without injecting the token.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:line 56 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore exits 0 silently when the marker is missing or empty instead of emitting `reason=marker_missing`.
  WHY: The contract test asserts that the diagnostic is present.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 57-59 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore exits 0 when `GH_TOKEN` is unset or empty.
  WHY: The contract test expects a nonzero result when the token is missing.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 21-23 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A second hide call exits 0 with a warning when an unrestored marker exists.
  WHY: The contract test expects a nonzero result to avoid discarding marker state.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:line 2727 (trap 'bash .../editor_git_credentials.sh restore' EXIT) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The EXIT trap and standalone syntax-repair restore step rely on the helper's exit code, which is 0 even when restore fails.
  WHY: Failed restoration is not detected directly, so subsequent Git operations proceed without a restore-failure signal.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 19-54 (hide action, entire) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The marker is stored in an editor-writable path, so the editor can delete or modify it.
  WHY: Restore reads the same marker path, allowing deletion or corruption to prevent or alter restoration.
